Lie group: Sophus Lie. Combining these two ideas, one obtains a continuous group where multiplying points and their inverses is continuous.
With the formula (CH3)2CO, this volatile solvent is produced by the millions of tonnes yearly, much of it to make precursors for plastics like bisphenol A — what is it?
Acetone (2-propanone or dimethyl ketone) is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CO.
The twelfth-brightest star in our night sky and the brightest in the constellation Aquila. It's one of the three vertices of the Summer Triangle asterism. Name this star.

Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky. It has the Bayer designation Alpha Aquilae, which is Latinised from α Aquilae and abbreviated Alpha Aql or α Aql.
The largest genus in the arum family with roughly 1,000 species, this flowering plant group is native to the Americas, ranging from northern Mexico down to northern Argentina — which genus?
Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.

This lung condition — the partial collapse of alveoli that reduces gas exchange, usually in just one lung — is a very common finding on chest X-rays, though it's technically distinct from a fluid-filled lung or a full pneumothorax — what is it?
Atelectasis is the partial collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange, more specifically the collapse of alveoli.
Native to Southeast Asia, the glossy heart-shaped leaves of this evergreen vine are chewed together with areca nut — name the plant?
Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Located in the head in most animals with nervous systems, this organ receives sensory information, generates thought and cognition, and coordinates the body's muscles and glands — name the organ?
Brain is an organ that serves as the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate and most invertebrate animals.
This Italian mastiff breed once hunted big game and herded cattle, and today mostly serves as a guard dog and loyal companion — name the breed?
Cane Corso is an Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
This English polymath is credited with inventing the first mechanical computer and designing an unrealized 'analytical engine' programmed using ideas borrowed from the Jacquard loom. Who is he?
Charles Babbage (26 December 1791 - 18 October 1871) was an English polymath.
Almost instantly after a vessel is injured, platelets swarm and fibrin cross-links to turn blood from liquid to gel, stopping the leak so repair can begin. What's the name for this clotting process?
Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.
Which vanilla-scented, benzopyrone lactone compound acts as a plant's chemical defense against predators and, via its derivatives, gave rise to the anticoagulant warfarin?
Coumarin is an aromatic organic chemical compound with formula C9H6O2.

This condition's four subtypes include one caused by kidneys that don't respond to a hormone called vasopressin and another linked to excessive fluid intake from a damaged thirst mechanism — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Born in Dublin in 1869 into an old Anglo-Irish scientific family, she's considered the very first woman to work as a medical physicist — who was she?
Edith Anne Stoney (6 January 1869 - 25 June 1938) was an Irish physicist.
This flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of just two species cultivated for their alkaloid-rich leaves — what is its scientific name?
Erythroxylum coca is a species of flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae.

Species in the stinging genus Solenopsis are sometimes confused with unrelated weaver insects in Southeast Asia that share their reddish color and painful bite — what's the common name for this group?
Fire ant are several species of ants in the genus Solenopsis, which includes over 200 species.
Its name literally means 'Earth writing,' and it explores not just where things are but how they changed and came to be across the planet — what field is it?
Geography (from Ancient Greek geographia; combining ge 'Earth' and graphein 'write', lit. 'Earth writing') is the study of the lands, features, inhabitants, and phenomena of planet Earth.

This small, hardy aquarium fish native to northeast South America gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs, and now ranks among the world's most widely kept tropical species — what fish is it?
Guppy (Poecilia reticulata), also known as the millionfish or rainbow fish, is a member of the family Poeciliidae and, akin to most New World members of the family, is classified as a livebearer.
This field studies the methods historians use — their sources, techniques, and theoretical approaches — in turning the past into an academic discipline — what's this field of study called?
Historiography is the study of the methods used by historians in developing history as an academic discipline.
This medieval Arab scholar, considered a forerunner of modern sociology and economics, wrote his most famous work, an introduction to history known as the Muqaddimah, in just six months — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 - 17 March 1406, 732-808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
This Brussels chemist ran a famous five-year willow tree experiment and coined the word 'gas' from the Greek for chaos — who was he?
Jan Baptist van Helmont (12 January 1580 - 30 December 1644) was a chemist, physiologist, and physician from Brussels.
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years pushing past skepticism to lay the groundwork for mRNA vaccines, winning a 2023 Nobel alongside Drew Weissman. Who is she?

Katalin Karikó (born 17 January 1955) is a Hungarian and American biochemist who specializes in ribonucleic acid (RNA)-mediated mechanisms, particularly in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA (mRNA) for protein replacement therapy.
Named for the German city where it was bred in the mid-19th century, this is a large German dog breed — which breed?
Leonberger is a German breed of large dog. The breed name derives from that of the city of Leonberg, in Baden-Württemberg, where it was bred in the mid-nineteenth century.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran but long grown in Europe, this herb's leaves, roots, and seeds are all used in cooking, tasting like a more intense mix of celery and parsley — what is it?
Lovage (Levisticum officinale) is a perennial plant, the sole species in the genus Levisticum in the family Apiaceae, subfamily Apioideae.
Cold-sensitive and tasting of sweet pine and citrus, this kitchen herb is so close to its cousin that in parts of the Middle East the two names are used interchangeably with oregano. What is it?
This Cuban engineer-turned-politician became his country's top leader in 2021, making him the first head of Cuba since the 1959 revolution who isn't a member of the Castro family — who is he?

Miguel Díaz-Canel (Latin American; born 20 April 1960) is a Cuban politician and engineer who has served as the 8th First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and the top leader of Cuba since 2021.
Diagnosed after a speech assessment, this condition can stem from psychological trauma or a neurological disorder and isn't always permanent — what is it called?
Muteness is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.

Made from unleavened dough rolled flat and then cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips, this staple food appears across cultures — in Italian cuisine, it goes by an entirely different name. What is it, generically?
Noodle are a type of food typically made from unleavened dough which is rolled flat and cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips or strings.
Often silent at first, this disease arises from an ovary or nearby structures and announces itself only later with bloating, pelvic pain, and abdominal swelling — what is it?
Ovarian cancer is a cancerous tumor of an ovary.
This flowering plant is the sole genus in its own botanical family and ranges from knee-high herbaceous perennials to woody shrubs over ten feet tall — what plant is it?
Peony is any flowering plant in the genus Paeonia, the only genus in the family Paeoniaceae.

This roundworm is one of the most common intestinal parasites in humans, causing a condition sometimes called oxyuriasis after the family it belongs to, and has also been found in bonnet macaques — what's the parasite?
Pinworm (parasite) (species Enterobius vermicularis), also known as threadworm (in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand) or seatworm, is a parasitic worm.

An Italian chemist and Auschwitz survivor, he wrote a celebrated memoir of his year in the camp and later a book of stories each named for a chemical element, hailed as the best science book ever — who was he?
Primo Levi (31 July 1919 - 11 April 1987) was a Jewish Italian chemist, partisan, Holocaust survivor and writer.
This Indian Air Force pilot became the first Indian ever to travel to space, flying aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission in 1984 — who is he?
Rakesh Sharma (born 13 January 1949) is an Indian cosmonaut and a pilot of the Indian Air Force.
This woody perennial flowering plant, genus Rosa in the family Rosaceae, includes over 300 species and tens of thousands of cultivars, with sharp prickles on many stems — name the flower?
Rose is either a woody perennial flowering plant of the genus Rosa, in the family Rosaceae, or the flower it bears.
This marine plant group includes kelp, captures carbon, and generates over half of the planet's oxygen — what is it called?
Seaweed refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
This discipline scientifically examines human society, scaling from micro-level individual interactions up to macro-level social systems — what is it?

Sociology is the scientific study of human society that focuses on society, human social behavior, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and aspects of culture associated with everyday life.

This eye disorder causes the eyes to misalign when looking at an object; if it develops in childhood it often leads to a 'lazy eye,' while adult onset usually causes double vision instead — what condition is it?
Strabismus is an eye disorder in which the eyes do not properly align with each other when looking at an object.

The primary male sex hormone and androgen, this hormone plays a key role in developing male reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics like muscle, bone mass, and body hair. What is this hormone?

Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.
Following the instructions of the genetic code, which cellular process decodes mRNA outside the nucleus to assemble a polypeptide chain?
Translation (biology) is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.

Named after an 18th-century Italian physicist and first published in 1797, this phenomenon explains why fluid pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrower pipe section — powering wine aerators and vacuum ejectors. What is it called?
Venturi effect is the reduction in fluid pressure that results when a moving fluid speeds up as it is funneled from one section of a pipe to another, smaller section.

Extracted from birch wood and named for the Greek word for 'wood', this white crystalline sugar alcohol is more soluble in water than any other common sugar alcohol except sorbitol. Name the compound?
Xylitol is an organic compound with the formula HOCH(CH(OH)CH2OH)2.
Taken by mouth, smeared as a cream, or injected, this antiviral medication is a frontline treatment for herpes simplex, chickenpox, and shingles. What is it?
Aciclovir: Antiviral medication used against herpes, chickenpox, and shingles.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, it clears out an alarming roll call of intestinal parasites — pinworm, hookworm, ascariasis, giardiasis and more. Which medication is it?
Commonly called buffalo, this large grazing mammal endemic to North America is one of just two living species in its genus, alongside a European cousin — what animal is it?
American bison: Species of bovid artiodactyl mammal.
Evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the Cretaceous, these insects are easily spotted by their elbowed antennae and slender, node-waisted bodies — what are they?
Ant: Family of insects. Nearly all ant colonies also have some fertile males called "drones" and one or more fertile females called "queens" (gynes).
Pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon in 2003, this mountaineer amputated his own forearm with a dull pocket knife to survive, later portrayed by James Franco in a film — who is he?
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy,' which term denotes a statement accepted as true without proof, serving as a starting point for further reasoning?
Axiom: Statement that is taken to be true.
A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid hiding in petroleum, this ring-shaped hydrocarbon helps give gasoline its distinctive aroma — what is it?
This crested songbird in the crow family sports a black, U-shaped collar and is known for hiding acorns to eat later — which eastern North American bird?
Blue jay: Species of bird. The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This rhythmic process of inhaling and exhaling delivers oxygen to the alveoli and removes carbon dioxide, with its per-minute rate counted as a vital sign — what is it?
Breathing: Process of moving air in and out of the lungs.
Found in chalk, limestone, eggshells, and pearls alike, this CaCO3 compound is also the active ingredient in agricultural lime and doubles as an antacid — what is it?
Calcium carbonate: Chemical compound. Materials containing much calcium carbonate or resembling it are described as calcareous.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
With independently swiveling eyes, a projectile tongue, and the ability to shift colors, this Old World lizard family is famous for camouflage — which reptile?
Chameleon: Family of reptiles. The members of this family are best known for their distinct range of colours, being capable of colour-shifting camouflage.
Named from Latin words meaning 'around' and 'day,' this roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle appears independently across animals, plants, fungi, and cyanobacteria?
Circadian rhythm: Natural internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
This bird family contains both doves and pigeons — including the feral rock dove common in cities — spanning 52 genera and 353 species worldwide. What's the family called?
Columbidae: Family of birds. The bird most commonly referred to as "pigeon" is the domestic pigeon, descendant of the wild rock dove, which is a common inhabitant of cities as the feral pigeon.

First published in 1785 by a French physicist, this principle holds that the electrostatic force between two charged particles is proportional to their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them — which principle is it?
Coulomb's law: Fundamental physical law of electromagnetism.

Originally bred for the hunt and later famous for trotting alongside horse-drawn firehouse carriages, this white breed with dark spots traces its roots to a region on the Adriatic coast — which breed?
Dalmatian dog: Croatian hunting/carriage/coach dog breed.
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.
Nicknamed the ALX, this Brazilian turboprop light-attack aircraft is assembled in Jacksonville, Florida with an American defense partner for low-threat counter-insurgency missions — which aircraft?
Embraer EMB 314 Super Tucano: Light ground attack and training aircraft.
Odorless, colorless, and dangerously sweet-tasting, this viscous compound goes into polyester fibers and antifreeze — and has even been spotted in outer space. What is it?
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.

Once classified as a subfamily of the seabasses, this diverse family of marine ray-finned fish is now treated as distinct, with most members drawn from two large genera. What are they commonly called?
Grouper: Family of fishes. The common name "grouper" is usually given to fish in one of two large genera: Epinephelus and Mycteroperca.
Nicknamed bindwood or lovestone, this clinging evergreen native to Europe scales tree trunks, walls, and fences — which plant?
Hedera helix: Species of flowering plant.

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)
It usually causes no symptoms at all, yet this persistently elevated arterial pressure is a leading cause of stroke, heart failure and premature death worldwide — what's the medical name for it?
Hypertension: Long-term high blood pressure in the arteries.

Marked by an IQ below 70 and deficits in everyday adaptive skills first apparent in childhood, this neurodevelopmental condition was formerly called 'mental retardation' in the U.S. — what is it now called?
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
These paired skin folds run from the mons pubis to the perineum and are considered the anatomical counterpart to the male scrotum — what are they called?
Labia majora: Folds of skin that contain and protect the vulva's other parts.
Also sold as Xylocaine, this amino-amide local anesthetic numbs in minutes and doubles as a treatment for dangerous ventricular heart rhythms — what is it?
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.
This French chemist's discoveries in fermentation and vaccination gave us a heat-treatment process that now bears his name and rabies and anthrax vaccines — who was he?
Louis Pasteur: French chemist, pharmacist and microbiologist (1822–1895)
In larger organizations it stacks into a pyramid, with a board and CEO at the top setting strategy — the broad practice of administering a business or government. What is it?
Management: Coordinating the efforts of persons.

Spanning everything from sacred religious writings to the exuberantly profane, and often grouped by place, language, and genre, what broad body of European writing falls between late antiquity and the Renaissance?
Medieval literature: Literary works of the Middle Ages.
Named from Greek words for 'small' and 'head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-average head size and can result from genetic syndromes or prenatal toxin exposure — what is it?
Microcephaly: Condition in which the head is small due to an underdeveloped brain.
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)
Made by giving a paper loop a half-twist before joining the ends, this non-orientable surface first appeared in Roman mosaics — what is it called?
Möbius strip: Non-orientable surface with one edge.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandins, though it carries a notable risk of liver problems — what is it?
Nimesulide: Anti-inflammatory drug. Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.
First described in 1689 by a local naturalist, this aquatic cave-dwelling salamander is the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordate native to Europe — what is it?
Britain, Germany, and Italy jointly built this twin-engine, variable-sweep-wing combat jet through a tri-national consortium, first flying it in 1974 — which aircraft?
Panavia Tornado: Family of multi-role combat aircraft.
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
Whether captured chemically on light-sensitive film or electronically by an image sensor, this art is fundamentally the practice of recording light — what is it?
Photography: Art and practice of creating images by recording light.
Whether natural silk or synthetic nylon, this class of polymer is defined by repeating units joined through amide bonds — what is it?
Polyamide: Macromolecule with repeating units linked by amide bonds.

Native to western Eurasia and a member of the rose family, this species — the wild or sweet cherry — is the ancestor of the sour cherry, though every part of the plant except its ripe fruit is mildly toxic. What is it called?
Prunus avium: Species of flowering plant in the rose family. The species is often cultivated as an ornamental tree.
Also known as hexogen, this nitroamine explosive is the key energetic agent in C-4 and a core ingredient of Semtex — which compound?
RDX: Explosive chemical compound. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
This branch of medicine handles more than 100 inflammatory diseases of the bones, muscles, and joints — like lupus and arthritis — and overlaps heavily with immunology. What is it?
Rheumatology: Medical speciality of inflammatory diseases.
Co-founder and first president of Mattel, she dreamed up a certain doll in 1959 and was later portrayed in the 2023 Barbie film — who was she?
Ruth Handler: American business magnate and inventor (1916–2002)
Exceeding 30 centimeters in length, this centipede from South America is the largest of its kind, preying on animals as large as small mammals and reptiles — which species?

Scolopendra gigantea: Species of Chilopoda (centipede). Scolopendra gigantea, also known as the Peruvian giant yellow-leg centipede or Amazonian giant centipede, is a centipede in the genus Scolopendra.
Made up of the collarbone, the scapula, and the upper-arm bone meeting in a ball-and-socket joint, which body part lets the arm swing in a full circle?
Shoulder: Part of the body. The articulations between the bones of the shoulder make up the shoulder joints.
This frozen dessert blends ice with fruit juice or purée — and sometimes wine, liqueur, or honey — for a refreshing icy treat. What is it called?
Sorbet: Frozen dessert. Sorbet is a frozen dessert made using ice combined with fruit juice, fruit purée, or other ingredients, such as wine, liqueur, or honey.
Whose pure-white winter coat became 'ermine,' the prized fur trimming the ceremonial robes of the UK House of Lords — and which was disastrously introduced to New Zealand? What animal is it?
Sometimes called gadflies, the females of this fly family bite land animals, including humans, to get the blood protein they need to produce eggs — which family?
Tabanidae: Family of insects. Horse flies and deer flies are true flies in the family Tabanidae in the insect order Diptera.
Often called the oldest form of drama, this collaborative art puts live performers before a live audience, blending gesture, speech, song, music and dance in one place — what is it?
Theatre: Collaborative form of performing art. The performers may communicate this experience to the audience through combinations of gesture, speech, song, music, and dance.
Located at either side of the back of your throat, these paired lymphoid organs form part of a defensive ring guarding the entrance to your digestive and respiratory tracts — what are they?

Tonsil: Lymphoid organs in the mouth and throat. The palatine tonsils and the adenoid tonsil are organs consisting of lymphoepithelial tissue located near the oropharynx and nasopharynx (parts of the throat).
Renowned as the greatest astronomer before the invention of the telescope, this Dane noticed an unexpectedly bright new star in 1572 and devoted himself to ever more precise instruments. Who was he?

Prized by the Inca, who reserved its ultra-fine wool for royalty alone, this wild Andean camelid is now believed to be the ancestor of the domesticated alpaca and is Peru's national animal — what is it?
Native to the high Himalayas, this large, shaggy bovine, scientific name Bos mutus, is the ancestor of the domesticated Bos grunniens — which animal?

While still a teenager, this French mathematician solved a 350-year-old problem about which polynomials can be solved by radicals, laying the groundwork for group theory, before dying from wounds suffered in a duel — who was he?
The symbol for neodymium is Nd. Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.

Harry Potter (film series): The series was produced and distributed by Warner Bros.

The Flash is a 2023 American superhero film based on the DC Comics character Barry Allen / The Flash.
